title: Finishing a tick blocks admission, so a multi-minute gate idles the whole window
description:
The dispatch window (5fx) admits an attempt as soon as a slot frees — it does NOT wait for a wave or a batch. But finishTick runs INLINE in runPlan's loop: collect, integrate, the integrated gate, then close. Admission only happens at the top of the loop, so for the whole of that leg the run admits NOTHING.

The gate is the expensive part: ~3m26s idle for the Go half, and today's measurements put it at 7-8 minutes on a loaded host. So every settled tick costs the window several minutes during which it runs one worker short AND starts nothing new.

Observed in epic dha, 2026-09-19: 6na settled at 22:25:40 and integrated at 22:26:11; its gate then ran while 15 wave-1 ticks were ready and three slots' worth of work sat unstarted. With 18 ticks in this epic, that is repeated per tick.

Note what is already right, so a fix does not undo it: excuseWindow keeps the OTHER live attempts polled and excused during a long finish (they are not declared dead), and a refusal still stops the run rather than draining it. The gap is admission only.

Work:
- Let the window admit while a settled attempt is being finished. The obvious shape is to run finishTick off the loop and keep the slot accounted for until it completes, so width is still honoured.
- Do not weaken the ordering guarantees: a tick is still gated against the integration branch as it stands when the gate runs, and a refusal must still stop the run before anything else integrates.
- Worth measuring first: how much wall clock a run actually loses to this. On an 18-tick epic at ~4 minutes a finish, the arithmetic suggests over an hour.

Related: 5fx (the window), w1j (what else the gate contends with).
notes:
2026-09-20 00:33 - 2026-09-19 — operator wants this now, for Phase 5's own throughput. Design agreed:

PART 1 (do first, small): the worker is FINISHED once its evidence is collected. Everything after — integrate, gate, close — is orchestrator bookkeeping, but finishTick disposes the worker LAST, so a worker slot is held for a worker that has already gone home. Dispose after collect and stop counting it against max_parallel; admit the next tick immediately. max_parallel bounds LIVE WORKERS (a model, a pane, CPU), not bookkeeping.

PART 2 (only if part 1 does not recover the wall clock): stop the finish blocking the loop, WITHOUT goroutines — internal/reconcile has zero by design and that is why a run is reconstructible. Make the finish a state machine the existing loop advances one step per round, as it already polls live attempts, which requires the gate to become start-and-poll rather than a blocking call. That would also give the gate its own bound and stall warning.

MUST NOT BREAK: finishing stays SERIAL (the gate judges the branch as it stands, and a refusal stops the run before anything else merges); excuseWindow keeps other live attempts polled and excused during a long finish; a newly admitted attempt still branches from the integration branch as it stands.
acceptance_criteria: A run admits new attempts while a settled attempt is being collected, integrated and gated, without exceeding the declared width and without weakening the refusal or gate ordering; the wall clock saved is measured on a real epic
